"No Beer Sold To Indians." A bar in one of the several frontier towns near the Fort Peck Dam construction site. By Margaret Bourke-White. Montana, 1936.

For their first ever cover story, Life sent Margaret Bourke-White to Montana to get some large scale photographs of the construction of the Fort Peck Dam, the world's largest earth filled dam. Instead they mostly got a photo essay about life in the frontier towns surrounding the dam.

“Hurry back, Maggie,” he said, and off I went. I had never seen a place quite like the town of New Deal, the construction site of Fort Peck Dam. It was a pinpoint in the long, lonely stretches of northern Montana so primitive and so wild that the whole ramshackle town seemed to carry the flavor of the boisterous Gold Rush days. It was stuffed to the seams with construction men, engineers, welders, quack doctors, barmaids, fancy ladies and, as one of my photographs illustrated, the only idle bedsprings in New Deal were the broken ones.

She did also manage to capture some images of the dam and Life featured this image on the front of their premiere issue.
